steps.label: Only temperature changes K
lines: Changes of concentration or pressure, and
the addition of a catalyst, shift or speed
the reaction but do NOT change the value of
Temperature is the only factor that changes
steps.why: K is defined at a stated temperature. Concentration and pressure changes move the system along the same K; only a temperature change moves K itself.
common_mistakes: Writing that adding reactant increases K. It shifts the position; K stays the same.
Quoting a K value without its temperature.
steps.memory_tip: Every K value is stated at a temperature. Change the temperature and K changes; no other factor changes it.
steps.margin_note: Position can shift for many reasons; the CONSTANT moves for one.

steps.label: The direction of the change
lines: For an endothermic reaction, K increases
For an exothermic reaction, K decreases

lines.text: Only a temperature change changes K — up for endothermic, down for exothermic

steps.why: Raising the temperature favours the direction that absorbs heat, so an endothermic forward reaction gains products and its K grows; an exothermic one loses products and its K falls.
common_mistakes: Writing that heating always increases K. The sign of ΔH decides the direction.
Mixing up the shift of position with the change of K — at a new temperature BOTH change.
steps.memory_tip: Raising the temperature increases K for an endothermic reaction and decreases K for an exothermic one.
steps.margin_note: Two lines, one for each sign of ΔH.
